en: The Yoga of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, in one fascicle. Compiled by the Duke of Sui,
Grand Master for the Pacification of the Court, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
with an appanage of three thousand households, invested with purple robes, posthumously titled Minister of Works and given the sobriquet Dajian (Great Mirror).
Now, in accordance with the Yoga system, as taught in the Vajraśekhara Sūtra,
I shall explain the maṇi-padmakula method of wish-fulfilling recitation;
by practicing this samādhi, one becomes like Avalokiteśvara.
First, he selects his disciples— those of noble lineage who revere the Dharma,
who are honored and beloved by many, who possess wisdom and courageous diligence,
and whose resolve in *vīrya* never abandons awakened insight.
Exhaustively practicing filial piety toward one’s parents, Possessing pure faith in the Triple Gem,
Joyfully cultivating the practices of bodhi, Without a moment’s interruption in the four immeasurable minds, And always delighting in the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, Revering the ācāryas and all noble beings,
A man of heroic vigor who has accomplished steadfast power, Well-versed in the gateway of yoga.
Always delighting in the practice of tranquility, possessing wisdom and fearlessness,
one constantly adorns the body with ethical discipline. Diligently cultivating the Secret Vehicle,
one respectfully relies upon the path of the *naya*, remaining single-mindedly without any stinginess.
Always delighting in hearing the sublime Dharma,
having entered samaya and received empowerment from a master, and having already been granted authorization,
one shall soon achieve accomplishment; such are the characteristics of this disciple.
Only then may the transmission be bestowed.
This is the wish-fulfilling jewel that can accomplish all activities.
As stated in the sūtras, the locations are mountain ranges and flowing waters, as well as pure aranyas.
In a mountain valley that accords with one's inclination, free from all dangers and fears, one should prepare offerings according to one's means.
Facing west, the practitioner [worships] Mañjuśrī, King of Sovereignty;
next, they pay homage to the Buddhas of the other directions.
Placing the five limbs upon the ground, having prostrated according to the instructions and knelt with both knees for a long time,
one should stand with palms joined and an open heart,
sincerely confessing all sins of the three karmas.
From past lives, I have wandered through birth and death;
now, before the Great Holy One, I repent with all my heart.
Just as the Buddhas of the past repented, so do I now.
May all sentient beings be completely purified by the power of this empowerment;
through this great aspiration, may self and others attain stainlessness.
The secret mantra is: [mantra].

Oṃ sarvathā viśodhaya sarvadharmān svabhāvaviśuddha haṃ. Next, the practitioner should rejoice in the merit and wisdom accumulated by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; they should contemplate the merits cultivated by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the past and give rise to joy, as if they themselves had performed them.
The roots of goodness accumulated by the Buddhas of the past, present, and future, as well as by the Bodhisattvas and all the holy ones— I join my palms and rejoice in them all,
just as if they were the roots of goodness I myself have accumulated, with a joy that is no different from my own.
Next, one should place the right knee on the ground and join the palms in the *padmaka* (lotus) gesture at the crown of the head,
visualizing that one is prostrating at the feet of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
The secret mantra is as follows:
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas with "Oṃ padma-vi-kṛti," one should sit at ease, either in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka),
the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
or the royal ease posture (rājopaveśa).
Having formed this mudrā of sitting, visualize Buddhas throughout the entirety of space,
each before oneself; abiding within those assemblies of noble ones,
from the knees upward, perform a whirling dance, joining [the hands] at the heart.
Like a lotus that has not yet blossomed, one should visualize and pay homage to all the Buddhas.
Next, bind the samaya seal: firmly clasp the thumbs and wisdom-fingers at the heart, with the middle fingers extended upward; this is the Vajra-Lotus Seal.
The Universal Holder of the Lotus, having already awakened the assembly of noble ones by forming this mudrā,
together with the Buddhas and the sons of the Sugatas—
those of great renown— graciously accepts [us] through sublime discernment.
Recalling my original vow made before the All-Illuminating Honored One,
and because I have not transgressed his instructions, I shall now empower [the practice] to bring it to fulfillment.
Next, form the Samaya-mudrā of the Peace, Delight, and Joy of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
The ten fingers are firmly bound; the thumbs and ring fingers are joined at their centers.
The hands of generosity and wisdom, as well as those of meditative concentration and insight, are each joined together and held upright.
The secret mantra says:
By displaying this mudrā, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas,
and Vajradharas are thoroughly and wondrously delighted.
Next, one should open the door of the heart and enter the syllable of vajra-wisdom.
Contemplate the two breasts: on the right is *tra* and on the left is *ṭa*, like the leaves of a palace door.
With the supreme vajra-bind, the three activities arise simultaneously; striking the heart, the two syllables open.
The mantra says:
"The seeds perfumed since beginningless time, And the accumulated afflictions—
now, with the mudrā of summoning sins, I gather them all in order to shatter them."
The ten fingers are firmly bound; the thumbs and ring fingers are extended like needles, while the index and middle fingers are bent like hooks.
Visualize summoning all sins, contemplating the various forms of those transgressions—hair standing on end, naked, black in form.
Furthermore, one should seal the heart; having touched it, one recites the secret mantra.
Because the three karmas are thus brought into correspondence, one is able to summon all accumulated sins.
Having performed this summoning through repeated recitation, one may then perform the rite of destruction.
The mantra is as follows:
Having summoned [the sins] into the palms, one then performs the rite of destruction.
With the hands joined in the previous mudrā, the fingers interlaced with the palms facing inward, one recites "MĀṂ" to bind all transgressions.
With both hands extended straight in the mudrā of patience and aspiration,
visualize the syllable *traḍ* as a vajra; clapping them together like the crushing of a mountain,
with wrathful speech and a furious form, one can purify all evil destinies.
Having recited [the mantra], one should clap with the mudrā of patience; for twenty-one repetitions as appropriate, the secret mantra is as follows:
"Because of this correspondence, it was taught by the skillful means of the Buddhas of the past."
The sins accumulated through the three karmas, And immeasurable, most heavy obscurations—
Having utterly destroyed these, they are like fire consuming dry grass.
Sentient beings are constantly deluded and confused, Failing to understand this essential principle.
Out of the Tathāgata’s great compassion, he opens this secret and wondrous gate.
Next, one should perform the seal of entry: firmly binding the two hands with the syllable *jñāna* of the Tathāgata within, the dhyāna and wisdom fingers enter into the center.
With the power of progress, the two [vowels] support each other in the manner of a ring;
visualize an eight-petaled lotus before you, upon which the letter A is placed, adorned with two points.
Because it is thus adorned, this wondrous syllable is properly named "A."
The color is white like crystal or snow, radiating a thousand rays of light.
Contemplating this with the power of the limb of exertion, one should hold the seed-syllable within the heart.
As the three karmas are applied in unison, recite this secret mantra:
Once one intends to enter it into the heart, the appearance of the syllable becomes increasingly radiant;
this is the very essence of the *dharmadhātu*. The practitioner should contemplate this, and before long will awaken to tranquility, for all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
The Tathāgatas of the three times, through the vajra body, speech, and mind,
employ sublime skillful means to hold [the seal] in the vajra-fist;
by thus closing the gates of the heart, one attains firmness through the syllable JÑĀ.
Then, bending the left arm forward and resting it upon the back of the wisdom hand,
one touches the chest with the seal; then, while the practitioner dwells in meditative equipoise, they recite this sublime mantra and firmly bind the two hands.
Placing [the hands] upward below the navel, with the thumbs and index fingers in the shape of a lotus—
this is called the *samādhi-mudrā*. Recite this secret mantra while exhaling and inhaling,
abiding in *ānāpāna* (mindfulness of breathing).
Visualize the Buddha pervading all of space; snap your fingers to awaken me, his son!
Why do you not realize that the Buddhas have attained unsurpassed perfect enlightenment through the wondrous Dharma of the true nature of reality?
Having been thus awakened by what he had heard, the practitioner spoke again:
"What is called 'reality'? I pray that the Most Victorious One will explain it;
may all the Buddhas be pleased. Thus he uttered these supreme words.
Excellent, Mahāsattva! You have been able to pose such a question.
Visualize within your heart the gateway of the syllable *a*, which enters into the mind; then recite this secret mantra:
Recite this silently once, and then, with the desire to increase one's diligence, visualize it as a lunar disc. Recite these sublime words again:
"It causes the lunar disc of the mind to become perfectly full and utterly pure."
Visualize a wondrous lotus in the center, with a precious vajra placed above it.
The secret mantra is:
"The measure of its extent is equal to space, pervading the three realms."
Furthermore, recite these wondrous words: The adamantine speech is free from sound;
herein one draws forth the sublime lotus. One emits thousands of blazing rays of light, and within each and every ray of light, are immeasurable buddha-fields.
Within the realm is a wondrous lotus; visualize one who holds a precious lotus and a supreme victory banner. From within the banner emerges a sublime sound:
"Whoever possesses even slight merit, may all their aspirations be fulfilled."
Abiding in this samādhi of tranquility for the benefit of all sentient beings,
such bodhisattvas as these remain in meditative equipoise;
from the womb of the lotus, they radiate a thousand wondrous rays of light.
All for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the pāramitās such as dāna enter universally into all samādhis; through the skillful gateways of their principles,
out of compassion for sentient beings, they employ immeasurable expedient means.
Manifesting in various emanations, from birth through to parinirvāṇa,
you turn the great and wondrous wheel of Dharma; all the sublime teachings spoken from the wish-fulfilling jewel of your mind are accomplished by means of this wheel.
Taking the wheel as sublime wisdom, it can sever all fetters and latent tendencies;
by turning the sublime Wheel of Dharma, this becomes the path of merit and wisdom.
Next, one correctly observes all things, gradually withdrawing the lotus of one's wisdom.
The mantra says:
All Tathāgatas wherever they may be enter into a single essence,
just as a clear mirror is able to manifest myriad images.
The essential nature of the dharmadhātu abides as a vajra-lotus,
which transforms into a precious lotus; it becomes the Cintāmaṇi held in the hand of the Bodhisattva Viśvapani, with six arms and a golden-colored body.
One should visualize oneself as seated upon the sovereign king of lions,
adorned with a crown of jewel-ornamented topknots; abiding in the posture of preaching the Dharma,
with the first hand held in the gesture of contemplation out of compassion for sentient beings.
The second holds the jewel of intention, capable of fulfilling all vows;
The third holds a rosary, for the sake of delivering beings from the suffering of the animal realm.
With his left hand he presses upon the Mountain of Radiance, Accomplishing immovability.
The second hand holds a lotus, capable of purifying all that is contrary to the Dharma;
the third hand grasps a wheel, capable of turning the unsurpassed Dharma.
With six arms and a vast body, you are able to traverse the six realms of existence.
Through the skillful means of great compassion, he observes the ascetic practices that sever the suffering of all sentient beings; seated within a lunar disc,
his body radiates a thousand beams of light, with a halo encircling both his neck and back.
Again, visualize the moon-disc of the mind, which also possesses a precious lotus flower; by this, one becomes firm and immovable.
Having contemplated the body as free from all deluded thoughts, recite this secret mantra:
Holding this Dharma as such, with the ten fingers joined like lotus petals and the arms bent like jewels,
one should visualize the syllable *HŪṂ* at the heart, forehead, throat, and crown, and place *TĀRA* upon the forehead.
The syllable *Kṛt* is at the throat; place the syllable *Aḥ* upon the crown.
By maintaining this visualization, this body becomes like a vajra.
Furthermore, recite this secret mantra: "The lotus-speech is sound."
Next, one should perform the consecration: The wise one joins the lotus-palms with the thumbs and forefingers in the shape of a jewel;
opening the ring fingers and little fingers, they are placed far apart at the forehead while reciting the secret mantra. One should visualize the Buddha conferring the consecration.
Then, with this sublime mudrā: place both hands apart at the sides as if binding a lotus garland;
slowly lower them forward while visualizing the gesture of trailing white ribbons. Recite these sublime words:
Next, one should bind the armor: from the heart, the two hands in the lotus gesture circle toward the back;
from the back, they circle toward the navel, then the waist and both knees, gradually ascending to circle behind the neck.
From the neck it should go to the throat; then, circling behind the head, it returns to the forehead;
finally, circling behind the crown of the head, it gradually descends forward as one recites this secret mantra.

To bring joy to all Buddhas, one should perform the Lotus-clapping mudrā by joining the two hands in the lotus-palms gesture; the secret mantra for clapping them skillfully to evoke delight is as follows:
Visualize before one’s own body that the syllable-hinge (hrīḥ) transforms into a lotus king;
within it is the syllable-hinge with the syllable-traṃ on both sides, serving as the vajra-jewel-lotus.
Together they transform into the Honored One; holding the *viśvavajra* and wonderful jewels as before, one visualizes oneself [as him].
Now, the visualization is likewise performed so that the two bodies may be non-dual. Next, perform the rite of summoning.
The ten perfections are like lotuses not yet in bloom;
with the power of progress, one should assume the posture of a hook and recite this secret mantra.
Having thus summoned the practitioner of the Lotus Sound, one should next form the noose mudrā.
As before, join the palms in the lotus gesture; with the index fingers and middle fingers joined like a ring, this is called the "Lotus Rope. It can fulfill all wishes.
One should recite this secret mantra to summon [the deity] into the wisdom body.
Having entered the body of wisdom, in order to prevent any wavering,
one should again bind the lotus-chain. One should form a mind of firm resolve as before,
joining the palms in the lotus gesture, with the thumbs and ring fingers pressed together like a ring.
The powers and wisdoms are likewise; their mutual connection is like a chain of hooks.
To bring about sublime joy, one should form the lotus-bell mudrā by holding the lotus with the palms joined, while the dhyāna and wisdom fingers enter into the center of the palms.
With the power of progress abiding like a circle, one should recite this secret mantra;
next, one should recite the hundred-syllable secret mantra of the Lotus Family and offer arghya water with saffron and white sandalwood.
With camphor and various flowers, hold them with both hands in offering.
Next, perform the inner and outer offerings; the so-called inner offering is the lotus-king:
place the *pāṇi* (palms) like a *kamala* (lotus) at the heart.
With the wisdom and dhyāna hands extended straight, this is called the Lotus Joy mudrā.
Next, perform the Flower Garland mudrā;
do not alter the previous Joy mudrā, but instead hold both hands forward as if offering it.
Visualize various jeweled garlands filling the entire realm of space;
the secret mantra is as follows.
Next, one should offer with the song mudrā to the Knower of the Wisdom Lotus.

Again, with the previously mentioned sublime mudrā, bend the palms and hang the fingers [representing] the perfections from the navel gradually up to the mouth; then release them downward in the manner of pouring,
while visualizing the sound of the kiṃnaras as making offerings to all the noble ones.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, one should form the dance mudrā: rotate the previous mudrā to the left and right, join the exquisite lotus-like palms, place them upon the crown of the head, and then release them.
Through these four offerings, one can attain great supernormal powers.
The mantra says:
By performing these four offerings, one can accomplish the most supreme matters.
Next, perform the outer offerings, presenting them with a joyful mind.
Directing the mind toward the boundless realms, this method of lotus incense offering was spoken by the true words of all Buddhas for the benefit of all sentient beings.
With the lotus-palms turned downward, like the gesture of burning incense,
recite these secret words while visualizing clouds of incense making offerings that pervade the entire realm of space, honoring all the assemblies of noble ones.
Next, one should form the Flower Mudrā; with the thirty-two marks, adorn all the Tathāgatas.
Visualizing clouds of flowers of wondrous color, extend the mind to pervade all things, joining the lotus palms as before.
Scattering above like a mass of flowers, I offer them to all the Tathāgatas and the sons of the Sugatas.
Visualize clouds of flowers filling the realm of space,
exquisitely fragrant and most magnificent, with jewel trees of supreme adornment.
Recite these secret words and employ the three karmas in unison.
Because sentient beings are shrouded by ignorance and separated from the light of wisdom,
one should form the Wisdom Lamp mudrā in order to purify them.
With the previous lotus-hand gesture, the dhyāna and wisdom fingers held close together,
visualize a maṇi lamp that illuminates the entire realm of empty space and emits immeasurable light; then recite this secret mantra:
Next, the wise one should form the mudrā of the Perfume of Liberation in order to purify sentient beings. Offering this perfume of śīla,
with both hands joined in the lotus-palms gesture, one should apply the perfume at the heart in the manner of the perfume-mudrā.
The ten perfections form the habitual perfuming; like an ocean of fragrance pervading space, one offers to the Buddhas and those who are honored.
Having performed the outer and inner offerings by reciting these secret words, one should then maintain right mindfulness.
Bind the Secret Root Mudrā. Having first recited the root mantra seven times clearly, place the palms together at the heart;
with the *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers joined like a lotus flower.
The power of progress has the form of a maṇi jewel; the remaining perfections are all like banners.
Recite the root mantra and contemplate the fulfillment of the wishes of sentient beings.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the heart-secret: according to the previous root mudrā, bind the thumbs, ring fingers, and middle fingers. This is called the Root Heart Mudrā;
it fulfills all intentions and whatever the mind contemplates.
By binding this mudrā, all mantras shall be accomplished.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the *anucitta-mudrā* (Mind-accordant Mudrā): with both hands, form a firm *vajra-bandha*.

The form of the Vajra-maṇi: the dhyāna and prajñā hands are extended side by side, the fingers of the śīla hands are likewise spread straight, and the dāna and prajñā hands are crossed and held upright.
Recite this heart-and-heart secret mantra:
Next, visualize that from the mouth of the Honored One,
the secret words flow forth clearly formed as syllables; rays of five-colored light,
intermingling with extraordinary hues, enter the mouth of the yoginī.
Visualize the mind within a lunar disc, as brilliant as red crystal;
contemplate each [syllable] with precise attention, following the principle and awakening accordingly.
Abiding in meditative concentration, practice and enter the gateway of the letter A.
One immediately enters the contemplation of the syllable Cakra (Wheel), observing all syllables everywhere;
this is called the mindfulness of samādhi. Through this correspondence, one attains wisdom and liberation, and before long, achieves the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñatā).
If one maintains constant mindfulness in accordance with the sound, abiding in the most supreme, wondrous,
and extraordinary visualization of the deity, one should not be impatient;
the mind should be neither too high nor too low, neither too lax nor too tense.
The wise one, free from conceptualization and all deluded thoughts,
If they recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, All that is sought will be accomplished.
With both hands holding a rosary made of crystal or lotus seeds.
One should string one hundred and eight conch beads, pearls, or other flawless, lustrous gems;
for each bead, recite the Heart Mantra and the Heart-of-the-Heart Mantra seven times, or the Vidyārājñī.
Having performed this rite of empowerment and strung the rosary,
one should pass each bead through the mind; chanting "svāhā" in unison,
recite it one thousand and eight times according to one's capacity.

Whether practiced four times or three times a day, this dharma is superior even to the *Sādhanamālā* (Ruyi Lun Jing) during the final watch of the night; as taught by the Buddha in the original scripture,
if one practices in this way, one will realize the first bhūmi in this very life.
After these sixteen lifetimes, one will attain unsurpassed bodhi;
how much more so regarding worldly siddhis! If in this present life things do not go as desired, recite according to one's capacity and then re-bind the samaya.
Furthermore, for the eight offerings: perform the two-fingered firm vajra-bind of the Lord of Secret Mantras;
extend the fingers in the shape of lotus petals from the heart to the face, and join the palms as a flower at the crown of the head.
Visualize the Honored One in the midst of space; then, having performed the ritual dismissal of the Noble One with the secret mantra,
return to the palace and abide in the visualization of one's own tutelary deity.
Or, in a quiet and secluded place, one should recite Mahāyāna sūtras such as the Laṅkāvatāra, the Avataṃsaka, the Prajñāpāramitā,
and the Tattvasaṃgraha, contemplating and practicing them accordingly.
Having recited the scriptures, whether walking, standing, sitting,
or even lying down to rest, if one does not interrupt the bodhicitta,
siddhi shall be attained before long; so it was said by Vajragarbha.
This ritual procedure for great compassion does not require selecting specific days,
lunar mansions, times, food, or bathing; whether pure or impure,
one should always practice it without interruption, remaining free from distraction.
In a secluded and tranquil place, without engaging in worldly affairs,
one should contemplate and make a vow; having formed the samaya-mudrā and paid homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, one may then walk back and forth as desired.
The Yoga of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, in one fascicle.
